QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_33

question.text: What happens when a clearing member defaults on their settlement obligations?

answer.text: The clearing corporation completes settlement through the guarantee framework, applying the defaulting member's monies first, then insurance (if any), then CC resources, before drawing on Core SGF components
All trades of the defaulting member are reversed
The exchange suspends trading for the day
RBI directly compensates the affected counterparties

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 251 of the NISM Series IV workbook, settlement is guaranteed even if a broker or clearing member fails to fulfil obligations. Pages 270-271 state that the Fund / Core SGF is used to complete settlement when a clearing member fails. Page 273 sets out the default waterfall: defaulting member monies first, then insurance if any, then CC resources, before Core SGF components are drawn upon. The Trap: Trades are not reversed; the clearing corporation guarantees settlement and continues to honour obligations to non-defaulting members. The exchange does not automatically suspend trading on default. RBI does not directly compensate affected counterparties. Note: Source-backed waterfall from pages 251 and 270-273 of Series IV: defaulting member monies, then insurance, then CC resources, then Core SGF components.
